# Final Touches — Murim Login

## Goal

Prepare one mastered chapter for readers. This pass adds footnotes, repairs formatting, and fixes duplicate or missing sentences. It is not a fluency rewrite.

Keep the mastered prose. Change a sentence only to attach a footnote, repair System / thought / speech / chat formatting, restore a source sentence the English dropped, or remove an English sentence the Korean does not support.

## Duplicates and omissions

Compare the English with the Korean source.

- Restore source facts, events, dialogue, and sentences the English dropped, in the same place in the scene.
- Remove English sentences that have no support in the Korean.
- Keep a bold label that names a quoted document, manual, warning, or sign, such as `> **Warning**`. Keep it when this chapter recalls or reprints a notice that was labeled earlier, even if the Korean reprint shows only the body.
- Keep repetition the Korean itself repeats: comedy, panic, emphasis, echoed dialogue, and short beats such as `……`.
- Do not treat a short refrain or a deliberate echo as a duplicate.

## Footnotes

Use Markdown footnotes (`[^1]`, `[^2]`, …). Number them in order of first appearance, starting at 1 for this chapter. Put every definition in one block at the end of the file.

Within this chapter, write one definition for a term, unit, amount, or reference. Every later occurrence of that same thing reuses the same marker. `goshiwon` five times is one note, and so is `hyung`. A different amount or a different term gets its own note. Another chapter may carry its own note for the same term.

Write notes in factual English. No spoilers and no jokes added by the note. Romanize words. A note may include the original character when it is explaining that character. Keep Hangul jamo already used as chat reactions, such as ㅋㅋ and ㄷㄷ.

Add a note only when an English reader would otherwise miss the meaning or the conversion. Skip it when the sentence already says what the reference means. A translated proverb whose warning is plain, a joke the next line completes, a place name used as a place, and a fictional law the dialogue already describes do not get notes.

Skip a conversion footnote when the prose already states both metric and imperial for that quantity.

### Won

Footnote Korean won, including round figures and vague amounts (“hundreds of millions of won”), when the prose does not already give the conversion. Use only the project rates in the packet. Show dollars, then euros, as approximate figures. Round large amounts to about two significant figures and say “about.” For a vague amount, give the approximate range those words cover. One note per distinct amount; reuse it for every later mention of that same amount.

Do not convert traditional money (nyang, taels, cash) or Chinese yuan with the won rate. Explain those with a cultural or historical note only when the English does not already carry the meaning.

### Units

Footnote a Korean or Chinese traditional unit, or a metric quantity, once in the chapter, with both metric and imperial, using this table:

| Unit | Use | Metric | Imperial |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| pyeong (평) | area | 3.31 m² | 35.6 ft² |
| geun (근) | Korean weight | 600 g | 1.32 lb |
| ja / cheok (자) | length | 30.3 cm | 11.9 in |
| chi (치) | length | 3.03 cm | 1.19 in |
| don (돈) | weight | 3.75 g | 0.132 oz |
| gwan (관) | weight | 3.75 kg | 8.27 lb |
| ri (리), Korea | distance | 393 m | 0.244 mi |
| li (里), China | distance | 500 m | 0.311 mi |
| jin (斤), modern Chinese | weight | 500 g | 1.10 lb |
| liang (两), modern Chinese | weight | 50 g | 1.76 oz |

Choose Korean ri or Chinese li from the setting. Say which one the note uses.

Also footnote metric quantities already in the English (kilometers, meters, centimeters, kilograms, grams, liters, square meters, degrees Celsius) with the imperial equivalent. Use unit words or abbreviations (`ft`, `in`, `mi`, `lb`, `oz`, `gal`). Do not use `"` or `'` as unit marks.

### Cultural references

Footnote a Korean, Chinese, or other Asian word, custom, institution, food, joke, or allusion when the English does not already carry it: `goshiwon`, `hyung`, `doenjang`, `jeonse`. Explain it in one or two sentences. One note per term in the chapter, reused by every later occurrence.

Leave it unnoted when the English is already clear. Do not explain a proverb the translation has already stated, a pun the scene completes, or ordinary vocabulary.

Do not footnote standing series vocabulary. Never add a note whose job is to define any of these, including ordinary variants and compounds:

- Murim
- qi, including demonic qi, innate qi, and qi deviation
- dantian, including the Upper, Middle, and Lower Dantian
- internal energy
- mana

A note about something else may mention these words. Do not attach a marker to them.

## Formatting

Enforce these four patterns. Repair System, speech, thought, and chat formatting when it drifts. Leave every other blockquote heading as it stands.

- **System.** Each real game System panel is one Markdown blockquote headed exactly `> **System**`. Keep the panel’s lines inside that blockquote. Start a new panel only when prose intervenes. Keep every `> **System**` panel from the mastered chapter, including a notice the narrator only hears. Do not turn a panel into italics, a sound effect, or narration. Do not wrap System text in square brackets or label a manual, sign, or ordinary quotation as System. A manual or remembered notice keeps its own label, such as `> **Warning**` or `> **Product User Manual**`. That label is not a System panel, and it is not drift.
- **Speech.** Spoken dialogue uses curly double quotes (`“` `”`). Not straight quotes, not italics.
- **Thoughts.** Direct thoughts are italics with no quotation marks. Keep a mastered thought in italics. Do not turn it into spoken dialogue.
- **Chat and comments.** Public comment threads and private chat logs shown as threads are one blockquote. Each message line begins with `└`, as in `> └ **Name:** message`. Keep a thread title that is not itself a message, such as `> **Peace Guild**`, on its own line above the messages. Do not add a `**Chat**` heading. A status line that is only a name or level, such as `> **Lv. 22 Hyuk Mujin**`, is not a chat message. Leave that line unchanged, including the bold. Ordinary spoken dialogue stays in curly quotes.
- **Headings.** The only Markdown heading is `# Chapter N`. Do not add `##` or `###`. A diary title or similar label stays a bold line, `**Training Day 1**`, even when the mastered copy used a smaller heading.

Leave narration as narration. Scene breaks stay `* * *`, with the same count as the source.

## Output contract

Return only the complete English Markdown chapter. The first nonblank line must be `# Chapter N`. No status line and no model preamble. Do not add Hangul syllables. Chat jamo and a character cited in a note may stay.

## Project conversion rates

These rates are binding. Do not look up or substitute a market rate.

- 1 US dollar = 1400 Korean won
- 1 euro = 1550 Korean won

Convert every won amount with these rates. In each footnote, give dollars first and euros second.

```text
＃242화



서글서글한 인상의 청년이었다.

나이는 많아 봐야 이십 대 중후반으로 보였고, 왠지 모르게 친근하게 느껴지는 미소가 입가에 맺혀 있었다.

“휴우, 발걸음이 왜 이렇게 빠르시오?”

“저 아세요?”

“모르오.”

“그런데 왜?”

“옷깃만 스쳐도 인연이라고 하지 않소?”

“아직 옷깃도 안 스쳤는데요.”

“대신 말을 섞었으니 상관없잖소. 나랑 친구 합시다.”

“…….”

둘 중 하나다. 미친놈이거나, 미친 인싸거나.

나는 찬찬히 청년의 모습을 훑었다. 펑퍼짐한 장포 아래 숨겨진 잘 발달한 근육과 허리춤에 비죽 튀어나와 있는 검자루를 눈으로 확인했다.

동시에 그의 몸 안에 도사린 기운을 느꼈다.

‘절정 고수네?’

실제 나이가 얼마나 될지는 모르겠지만 제법 뛰어난 성취다.

아니, 이 정도면 대단하다고도 할 수 있다. 이십 대에 절정의 경지에 오른다는 것은 그만큼 어려운 일이니까.

하지만 뭐랄까, 순간 눈앞의 청년에게서 느꼈던 기운은 딱 그 정도였다.

굳이 표현하자면…….

‘평범한 절정 고수?’

절정 고수라면 이미 대단한 경지인데도 평범하게 느껴지는 이유는, 주위에 하도 괴수들이 넘쳐나서다.

무려 진무경에 청풍, 화왕이라는 정신 나간 삼단 콤보를 맞으면 이런 후유증도 생기는 법이지.

어쨌건 파악은 대충 끝났다. 나는 청년에게 정중하게 말했다.

“신경 쓰지 말고 갈 길 가쇼.”

“허어, 친구 사이에 너무 매정한 거 아니오!”

“친구면 반말해도 돼요?”

“허허. 물론일세!”

“그럼 꺼져. 새꺄.”

“…….”

그대로 청년을 뒤로하고 걸어가기 시작했다. 잠시 굳어 있던 그가 종종걸음으로 빠르게 따라붙는다.

“생전 처음 듣는 폭언이라 순간 정신이 멍해졌군. 좋아, 이런 게 진짜 친구지!”

“곱게 말할 때 가라, 그냥.”

“자네는 이름이 뭔가?”

“마이클 존슨.”

“특이한 이름이군.”

“……그걸 믿냐?”

“장삼? 아니면 유필? 혹시 구파일방이나 오대세가의 제자인가?”

“그게 왜 궁금한데?”

“그야 관심이 있어서 아니겠나. 적살부를 일격에 죽였다며?”

낯선 별호에 발걸음이 우뚝 멈췄다.

“누구?”

“흑산채의 채주 말일세. 자네 솜씨 아닌가?”

나는 오던 길에 해치웠던 털북숭이 산적 두목을 떠올렸다. 워낙 머릿수가 많아 기선 제압을 위해 제일 먼저 처리한 놈이었다.

어쩐지 산적치고는 강하다 싶었는데, 제법 이름이 있는 놈이었던 모양이다.

“그런데 그걸 어떻게 알았지?”

“아까 객잔에서 금와상단의 상인들에게 들었네. 살아남은 산적들이 철구와 사슬을 든 괴인의 짓이라고 했다던데?”

청년이 활짝 웃으며 내 등에 고정된 철구들을 가리켰다.

이상한 오해를 살 것 같아 천으로 덮어 짐처럼 위장했는데, 역시 절정 고수의 눈썰미를 속일 수는 없었나 보다.

“한데 마침 자네가 지나가고 있지 않겠나. 흥미가 동해 냉큼 따라왔지.”

“흠.”

“그래서 이름이 어떻게 되나?”

말해 줄까, 말까.

잠깐 고민하다가 입을 뗐다. 나도 이 괴짜 청년이 어느 문파의 누구인지 슬슬 궁금해지기 시작했기 때문이다.

“진태경. 그게 내 이름이다.”

“혹시 산서성 태원진가의 그 진태경?”

“날 알아?”

“알다마다. 산서잠룡이 화왕의 제자로 들어갔다는 소문을 귀에 못이 박이도록 들었는데.”

일 년은 짧다면 짧고, 길다면 길다.

그러나 나와 화왕에 관한 소문이 대륙 전역에 퍼지기에는 충분한 시간이었다.

“그러는 그쪽은?”

“아, 본인은…….”

청년이 씩 웃으며 말을 이었다.

“종리추. 운남(雲南)에서 온 종리추라고 하네. 사문을 밝히지 못하는 건 사정이 있으니 양해해 주게.”

“운남의 종리추?”

“별호는 상승검(常勝劍)일세. 혹시 들어 본 적 있나?”

운남이라는 지명은 알지만 이름과 별호는 처음 들어 봤다.

지난 일 년간 열화동에 처박혀 있었으니 당연하다면 당연한 일이다.

“미안하지만 잘 모르겠는데.”

“그런가? 뭐, 모를 수도 있지.”

긍정적인 것 보소. 보통 저 나이대의 무인이라면 실망할 법도 한데, 전혀 그런 기색이 없다.

긍정 빌런이 진지한 얼굴로 말을 이었다.

“왜냐하면 지금 막 지은 별호거든. 항상 이기는 검객. 멋있지 않나?”

“…….”

미친놈인가.

순간 말문이 막힌 내게 종리추가 손목을 꺾는 시늉을 해 보였다.

“어떤가? 친구가 된 기념으로 술이나 한잔하는 것이.”

“딱히 생각 없어. 근처 객잔에는 자리도 없고.”

“무슨 소리. 자네 따라다니면서 쭉 봤는데, 한두 자리 정도씩은 꼭 비어 있더구먼.”

“……점소이가 자리 없다던데.”

“응? 그런데 왜 나한테는 빈자리 있으니까 들어오라고 했지?”

“…….”

젠장. 그럼 그렇지. 아무리 성라대연이 코앞이라고 해도 수십 개가 넘는 객잔 중에 빈자리가 하나 없는 것이 말이 되나.

‘내가 더러워서 씻는다. 더러워서.’

개울물이라도 떠서 씻어야지, 이러다가는 멀쩡한 객잔 놔두고 길거리에서 노숙하게 생겼다.

“괜찮은 객잔 하나를 알고 있으니 같이 가세. 친구가 된 기념으로 술값은 내가 내지.”

“친구는 무슨. 종리추라고 했었지? 너도 이제 갈 길 가라.”

내가 돈 한 푼 없는 빈털터리도 아닌데, 괜히 이상한 놈과 엮여서 노닥거릴 생각은 없다.

이 길로 쭉 가면 하천이 흐른다고 했던가?

기억을 더듬어 발걸음을 옮기는 내게 종리추가 물었다.

“이보게, 어디 가는 건가?”

“알 거 없다. 따라오지 마.”

“그럼 마지막으로 하나만 대답해 주게! 어디 가면 자넬 다시 볼 수 있지?”

“성라대연.”

그 대답이 마지막이었다. 나는 경공(輕功)을 발휘하여 빠르게 자리를 벗어났다. 순식간에 백여 장의 거리를 주파한 내 등 뒤로 종리추의 외침이 울려 퍼졌다.

“다음에 보세!”

싫어, 인마.



* * *



한 사람은 떠났고, 한 사람은 남았다.

종리추는 진태경이 사라진 방향을 바라보며 중얼거렸다.

“산서잠룡 진태경이라…….”

이내 주름 하나 없는 매끈한 입가에 보조개가 푹 패였다.

한동안 홀로 서서 실소를 흘리던 그는 얼마 떨어지지 않는 객잔으로 발걸음을 돌렸다.

일각 전, 진태경을 쫓아낸 점소이가 함박웃음을 지으며 허리를 굽혔다.

“어서 옵쇼!”

“남는 자리가 있나?”

“어이구, 물론입죠.”

종리추의 웃음이 한층 더 짙어졌다.

“……”

“That was the first time anyone has ever insulted me. I was stunned for a moment. Yes, this is what true friendship is!”

“Just go while I’m still asking nicely.”

“What’s your name?”

“Michael Johnson.”

“That’s an unusual name.”

“……You believe that?”

“Jang Sam? Or Yu Pil? Are you perhaps a Disciple of one of the Nine Sects and One Gang or the Five Great Families?”

“Why do you care?”

“Because I’m interested, of course. I heard you killed the Red-Killing Axe with One Strike.”

I stopped dead at the unfamiliar epithet.

“Who?”

“The Stronghold Lord of Black Mountain Stronghold. Was that your doing?”

I recalled the hairy bandit chief I had dealt with on the way here. There had been so many bandits that I had taken him out first to intimidate the rest.

I had thought he was unusually strong for a bandit. Apparently, he had been somewhat famous.

“But how did you find out?”

“I heard it from the Geumwa Merchant Group’s merchants at the inn earlier. They said the surviving bandits claimed it was the work of a strange man carrying iron balls and chains.”

The young man beamed as he pointed to the iron balls strapped to my back.

I had covered them with cloth to disguise them as luggage, since I did not want to invite any strange misunderstandings. But apparently, I could not fool the eyes of a Peak master.

“And then you happened to walk by. My curiosity got the better of me, so I came straight after you.”

“Hmm.”

“So, what’s your name?”

Should I tell him or not?

After a moment’s thought, I opened my mouth. I was beginning to grow curious about which sect this eccentric young man belonged to as well.

“Jin Taekyung. That’s my name.”

“Are you the Jin Taekyung of the Jin Family of Taiyuan in Shanxi Province?”

“You know me?”

“Of course I do. I’ve heard so much about the Sleeping Dragon of Shanxi becoming the Fire King’s Disciple that my ears are ringing.”

A year could be short or long, depending on how you looked at it.

But it was more than enough time for rumors about me and the Fire King to spread throughout the continent.

“What about you?”

“Ah, as for me…”

The young man grinned and continued.

“Jongni Chu. I’m Jongni Chu from Yunnan. I have my reasons for not revealing my sect, so I hope you’ll understand.”

“Jongni Chu from Yunnan?”

“My epithet is the Always-Victorious Sword. Have you ever heard of me?”

I knew Yunnan, but this was my first time hearing his name or epithet.

Considering I had spent the past year holed up in Fire Gate Cavern, that was only natural.

“Sorry, but I haven’t.”

“Is that so? Well, it’s understandable that you wouldn’t know.”

Would you look at that positivity? Most martial artists his age would have been disappointed, but he showed no sign of it.

The freakishly positive guy continued with a serious expression.

“That’s because I just came up with the epithet. A swordsman who always wins. Isn’t it cool?”

“……”

*Is he crazy?*

As I stood there speechless, Jongni Chu made a motion of twisting his wrist.

“How about it? Shall we have a drink to celebrate becoming friends?”

“Not interested. Besides, there aren’t any seats at the nearby inns.”

“What are you talking about? I’ve been following you this whole time, and every inn had at least one or two seats open.”

“……The waiters said there weren’t any.”

“Hm? Then why did they tell me there were empty seats and invite me inside?”

“……”

Damn it. Of course.

Even with the Star-Array Grand Banquet right around the corner, how could every last seat in dozens of inns possibly be taken?

*I’m washing because I’m filthy. Because I’m filthy.*

I would have to draw water from a stream and wash myself. At this rate, I would end up sleeping on the street despite leaving perfectly good inns unused.

“I know a decent inn, so come with me. I’ll pay for the drinks to celebrate our new friendship.”

“What friendship? You said your name was Jongni Chu, right? You should go on your way too.”

It was not as though I was completely penniless. I had no intention of getting tangled up with some weirdo and wasting time chatting.

Hadn’t someone said there was a stream if I kept following this road?

As I searched my memory and walked on, Jongni Chu called after me.

“Hey, where are you going?”

“None of your business. Don’t follow me.”

“Then answer just one last question! Where can I see you again?”

“The Star-Array Grand Banquet.”

That was my final answer. I used qinggong[^1] and quickly left the area. After covering more than a hundred zhang[^2] in an instant, I heard Jongni Chu shouting behind me.

“See you next time!”

*Not a chance, punk.*

* * *

One man left, and one remained.

Jongni Chu stared in the direction Jin Taekyung had disappeared and murmured,

“The Sleeping Dragon of Shanxi, Jin Taekyung…”

Before long, a deep dimple formed beside his smooth, unlined mouth.

After standing there alone and chuckling to himself for a while, he turned toward an inn not far away.

The waiter who had driven Jin Taekyung off fifteen minutes earlier bent at the waist with a broad smile.

“Welcome!”

“Do you have any seats left?”

“Of course, sir!”

Jongni Chu’s smile deepened.

* * *

Splash!

When I sat up, the hot water filling the wooden tub sloshed around me.

I had found the battered old tub lying in the grass, filled it with cold stream water, and heated it with Scorching Yang Qi.

After dumping and refilling the water several times to scrub away the accumulated grime, I felt as though I had lost several kilograms[^3].

“I feel like I’ve undergone Bone Transformation[^4].”

I finally felt alive again.

It would have been nice to have shampoo or body wash, but this was more than enough to satisfy me.

The inventories for Murim and the modern world were separate, so bringing any over had been impossible from the start.

*But these clothes are a problem.*

I frowned as I put the rags back on. It was hard to tell whether they were clothes or garbage.

The discomfort was one thing, but putting these back on made the bath feel completely pointless.

I wandered through the streets, intending to buy at least one cheap set of clothes.

The streets of Henan had been crowded with people from every class and profession even a year ago, but given the timing, martial artists were especially conspicuous now.

Naturally, snippets of their conversations reached my ears.

“Have you heard? The Sword Dragon of the Nangong Family won’t be participating in this year’s Star-Array Grand Banquet.”

“Good heavens. Why would the Sword Dragon suddenly drop out? Is there some sort of problem?”

“Who knows? It’s a shame. He was one of the favorites to win. The outcome is getting harder and harder to predict.”

“Among the young prodigies, the Ten Dragons and Phoenixes probably have the best chance, but…the age limit is thirty-five. There’s no telling what will happen.”

“That’s a fair point. The world is vast, and there are many masters. A powerful newcomer from outside the Nine Sects and One Gang or the Five Great Families could easily appear.”

“You mean someone like the Heaven Shaking Sword of the Jin Family of Taiyuan and the Sleeping Dragon of Shanxi?”

“Exactly. Though I don’t know whether either of them will attend this year’s Star-Array Grand Banquet.”

Hearing them talk about me made my face burn.

I quickened my pace and left the road behind.

As soon as I reached a main street lined with large buildings, a cloth shop displaying silk and dozens of different outfits caught my eye.

“Excuse me.”

“Why, they say clothes make the woman, but those suit you wonderfully. Are you perhaps a fairy? A fairy… What do you want?”

The cloth-shop employee had been enthusiastically showering a group of pretty female customers with flattery, but he frowned the moment I called out to him.

The change in his expression was so extreme that I barely resisted punching him in the face.

“Why do you think I came to a cloth shop?”

“To beg, obviously.”

“……”

No matter how ragged my clothes were, there was no hiding my massive frame.

If anything, the rags left so much skin exposed that my muscles stood out even more.

When I stared at him while subtly tensing my body, the employee flinched.

“W-why are you looking at me like that? Was I wrong?”

“That’s enough of the kind of remark you’ll regret. Let me see some clothes.”

“C-clothes?”

“Here. I have money, so don’t treat me like a beggar.”

The employee’s expression changed when I pulled out a silver nyang[^5] and waved it around.

Contrary to my expectations, it changed for the worse.

“That’s all?”

“It is. Is there a problem?”

“Good grief. What kind of clothes do you think you can buy with one lousy silver nyang[^5]?”

“……One lousy silver nyang[^5]?”

Had there been some major currency reform in the past year that caused the value of silver to collapse?

As I stood there in confusion, the employee snorted.

“Did you even read the price list before coming in?”

I reflexively turned and checked the sign.

A wooden board at the front of the shop had these words written across it in enormous letters:

> **The owner has gone mad! Star-Array Grand Banquet special discount! Martial-artist’s outfit—two silver nyang[^5]!**

“……Two silver nyang[^5]? For a martial-artist’s outfit?”

“With that, you could buy underwear at best. Our cloth shop handles only the finest silk. Even our martial-artist’s outfits are made from Shu brocade[^6].”

“……”

*So this was a department-store brand.*

Of all the places I could have walked into, I had chosen this one. What an embarrassment.

The other employees and customers inside the shop began whispering as they watched me.

“Oh my, he must be a beggar. How pitiful. Don’t you agree, dear?”

“He certainly looks like one. He seems strong enough to put those muscles to use, though. Should we take him in as a servant?”

“You’re so merciful, dear. I’m sure that beggar would be delighted.”

Being called a beggar was irritating enough, but hearing it from a couple made me twice as angry.

I shouted with all the anger I could muster.

“Who are you calling a beggar?”

“Gasp!”

“Eek!”

“H-how dare you!”

People recoiled in fright at my booming shout.

At the same time, several burly employees came rushing over and surrounded me, brandishing clubs threateningly.

“You bastard! How dare you make a scene here!”

“Do you even know where you are, you filthy beggar?”

“What? A beggar? Oh, you sons of bitches…”

*Fine. You said it.*

I rolled up the sleeve that was already half torn off.

“All right, let’s be a real pain in the ass today. Who owns this place?”

That was when it happened.

“You’re the kind of bastard who won’t come to his senses until he sees a coffin. How dare you make a scene here?”

A grave voice rang in my ears.

I slowly turned around and saw a man.

He wore a bamboo hat pulled low over his face and black silk clothes embroidered with dragons. One hand rested on the hilt of his sword as though he might draw at any moment.

The lips visible beneath the bamboo hat curled as he let out a quiet laugh.

“You seem to have learned a move or two somewhere, but if you don’t want to see blood, step aside.”

I cocked my head.

“And if I don’t?”

“Nameless martial artist, the price of reckless bravado is death.”

The people nearby erupted in cheers at the line straight out of a martial-arts movie.

Once the cheering died down, I spoke.

“Hey, can I ask you one thing?”

The martial artist answered casually,

“Speak. They will be your last words.”

I stared into the shadow beneath the martial artist’s bamboo hat and continued.

“You’re Hyuk Mujin, right?”

“……!”

I let out a deep sigh and looked up at the sky. A signboard written in vigorous, soaring calligraphy caught my eye.

**Hyuk Family Cloth Shop**

“You have three seconds. Put your head on the floor.”

[^1]: Qinggong is a martial-arts skill for moving swiftly and lightly.

[^4]: Bone Transformation refers to an advanced bodily transformation in martial-arts fiction.
